subject: Sentinel Analytics integration: technical acceptance sprint & signoff
messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex@sentinel.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Nadia Lopez <nadia.lopez@sentinel.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Jul 2028 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood partner validation kickoff — reference architecture & acceptance criteria

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the intro call last week. As discussed, Sentinel would like to run a short technical acceptance sprint (2 sprints — 1 week each) to validate our connector into Redwood Inference for model serving and telemetry ingestion.

Goals for the sprint:
- Validate TLS/mTLS setup for model API calls
- Verify token routing and rate-limiting behavior for our multi-tenant env
- Exercise prefix caching and KV cache interaction for streaming workloads
- Confirm log/event schema for audit/usage ingestion

I've attached our current reference architecture and a proposed OpenAPI contract. Can we schedule a 90-minute workshop this week with your SE and security leads to walk the runbook and confirm test cases?

Proposed attendees: Priyom (partner lead), Sergio (SE), Kimberly (security), Marissa (partner ops), Nadia (Sentinel eng), me.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this over the line.

Best,
Alex Chen
Head of Integrations, Sentinel Analytics
sentinel.ai

Attachments:
- sentinel_arch_diagram.pdf (diagram)
- api_contract_openapi.yaml (OpenAPI v3)
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex@sentinel.ai>
Cc: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 2 Jul 2028 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood partner validation kickoff — reference architecture & acceptance criteria

Alex — thanks, this looks good. I'm looping in the folks who will own the validation activities and the security review.

Sergio — can you lead the technical runbook review and own the API contract validation? I expect 3 test vectors: low-latency inference (streaming), high-throughput batch, and failure/retry semantics.

Kimberly — we'll need your eyes on the mTLS and logging schema; Sentinel is requesting retention/ingestion details for audit logs.

Marissa — coordinate SOW/timeline with Nadia and send a calendar invite. We can do Wed 10am PT for the 90-min workshop — works for everyone?

I'll take the action to draft the acceptance checklist after the workshop.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Partner Solutions Lead
Redwood Inference

From: sergio_alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Chen <alex@sentinel.ai>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 3 Jul 2028 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood partner validation kickoff — reference architecture & acceptance criteria

Thanks team — I'll run the runbook review in the workshop. High-level notes ahead of Wed:

- API contract: Redwood supports standard Bearer token + optional mutual-TLS; we'll validate both flows. If they present a client certificate workflow, we'll test rotation and fallback to token.
- Latency tests: we'll define 3 SLAs to validate (p50/p95/p99) for 256-token streaming and 1024-token batch. Sergio will own the script and shared harness.
- Caching: need to confirm how Sentinel keys prompts; if keys include session IDs we may need prefix normalization to get KV cache hits. We'll provide a small patch to simulate prefix collisions.
- Telemetry: Redwood emits structured events to our internal audit pipeline; we'll provide a mapping file. Sentinel needs to confirm field names for user_id, request_id, and model_variant.

I'll upload the preliminary test harness and a short runbook to the Drive link Priyom shared after the workshop.

— Sergio
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment mentioned: preliminary_test_harness.tar.gz (stub)
From: Alex Chen <alex@sentinel.ai>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, nadia.lopez@sentinel.ai
Date: Thu, 4 Jul 2028 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood partner validation kickoff — reference architecture & acceptance criteria

Sergio — appreciate the pre-read. A couple quick clarifications before the workshop:

- On token vs mTLS: Sentinel prefers token rotation + 1-hour TTL but can support mTLS for customers requiring cert-based auth. We'll bring both configs to the lab.
- On prefix normalization: our SDK currently includes session_id in the first-token; we can branch a build that strips session metadata for cache keys to exercise your KV cache.
- Telemetry fields: we'll align field names but we need a sample JSON schema for the audit events you emit. Can Kimberly share that during the call?

Nadia and I will prepare the two harnesses and a short smoke test matrix. See you Wednesday.

Thanks,
Alex
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: Alex Chen <alex@sentinel.ai>, nadia.lopez@sentinel.ai
Date: Tue, 9 Jul 2028 14:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood partner validation kickoff — reference architecture & acceptance criteria

All — workshop notes attached and acceptance checklist draft is below. Nice progress in the lab.

Acceptance checklist (draft):
- API auth: token rotation verified OR mTLS handshake validated
- Rate limiting: 95% of requests within agreed rate bands under 3 trials
- Latency: p95 for 256-token streaming < 220ms, p95 for 1024-token batch < 700ms
- Cache behavior: prefix-normalized workload shows >= 35% KV cache hit improvement
- Telemetry: audit events match field schema and appear in our ingestion pipeline
- Failover: graceful fallback to compatible model variant on simulated OOM

Next steps:
- Sentinel to provide signed SOW and PoC acceptance signoff (DocuSign link sent).
- Sergio to finalize test harness and upload final artifacts to Drive.
- Kimberly to attach the audit JSON schema and comment on retention limits.

Attachments:
- sentinel_test_plan.xlsx
- acceptance_checklist_v1.docx

Marissa Cole
Partner Programs
Redwood Inference
